text:
Mutation testing provides a useful foundation, but detection must be demonstrated rather than inferred from diagnostic coverage. [DeepCrime](https://zenodo.org/records/5082873) derives mutations from real deep-learning faults; [MuFF (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09846) studies stable, sensitive post-training mutation testing. For this toolkit, a proposed adaptation is paired diagnostic executions of the same frozen NextItNet checkpoint: inject wrong left-padding readout, future-context access, or history-independent features individually; include unchanged and no-op-patch controls. Report detection rate by fault, false alarms on controls, and component-localization accuracy. These are proposed measurements, not established results. A future-token perturbation should leave earlier causal features unchanged; left-padded readout should select the final nonpadding position, never count−1. History sensitivity alone does not establish useful personalization.

Leakage warrants explicit checks: [Le, Liu and Medlar (RecSys 2025)](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/dont-get-ahead-of-yourself-a-critical-study-on-data-leakage-in-of/) report sampled nDCG@10 reductions of 21.7–73.4% under a leakage-preventing evaluation split. This motivates auditing information access while preserving the supplied benchmark splits. Sampled-versus-full-catalog disagreement is independently well established: [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampling fidelity and robustness. Compare paired target ranks and hit disagreements on permitted diagnostic examples, keeping candidate construction explicit. Such probes cannot establish pinned validation HR@10; leave the host’s 99-negative evaluator unchanged and authoritative for selection.
